title: The derived base change map is computed by Cech complexes
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, let $g:T=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to S$, let $f:X\to S$ be a separated quasi-compact morphism of schemes, and let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $X_T=X\times_ST$ be the base change [def-pc-base-change], with projections $p:X_T\to X$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$, and $\mathcal G_T=p^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $\theta:Lg^*Rf_*\mathcal G\to Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T$ [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pc-derived-direct-image] be the base change map, i.e. the adjoint for $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ of the map $Rf_*\mathcal G\to Rf_*Rp_*p^*\mathcal G=Rg_*Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T$ induced by the unit $\mathcal G\to p_*p^*\mathcal G\to Rp_*p^*\mathcal G$. Choose a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^tU_i$, write $U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j$, let $K^\bullet$ be the alternating Cech complex of $A$-modules with $K^q=\prod_{|J|=q+1}\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)$, and let $K_T^\bullet$ be that of the cover $X_T=\bigcup_i U_i\times_ST$ for $\mathcal G_T$, so that $Rf_*\mathcal G\cong\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ and $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T\cong\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$ by [lem-pc-cech-resolution]. Then the maps $c_J:\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)\otimes_AB\to\Gamma(U_J\times_ST,\mathcal G_T)$, $s\otimes b\mapsto b\cdot(p^*s)|_{U_J\times_ST}$, commute with the Cech differentials and so form a cochain map $\gamma:K^\bullet\otimes_AB\to K_T^\bullet$, and under these identifications $\theta$ equals the composite $Lg^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}\to g^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}=(K^\bullet\otimes_AB)^\sim\xrightarrow{\tilde\gamma}\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$, the first arrow being the canonical map from the derived to the underived pullback.

source.place: node lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module, ## Proof, final comparison (cf. Stacks 08IB proof)

proof.text: The hypotheses on $S$, $X$, and the finite affine cover give the Cech resolution for $f$ by [lem-pc-cech-resolution]. The base changes preserve separatedness and quasi-compactness by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], and the opens $U_i\times_ST$ are affine, so the same Cech-resolution statement applies to $f_T$. For an intersection $U_J$, the morphism $U_J\to S$ is affine; [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] gives that $f_*j_{J,*}(\mathcal G|_{U_J})$ is quasi-coherent and identifies its sections on affine opens with $\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)$, which is the term used in $K^\bullet$ (and similarly after base change). The derived pullback and derived direct-image definitions supply the functors used in these identifications. Thus $Rf_*\mathcal G\cong\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ and $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T\cong\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$.

source.place: Proof, final comparison: Cech resolutions for X and X_T

proof.text: For each affine intersection $U_J=\operatorname{Spec}(C_J)$, the affine pullback-sections lemma [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], applied to $f=p$, $V=U_J$, and $U=p^{-1}(U_J)$, gives an isomorphism $c_J:\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)\otimes_{C_J}(C_J\otimes_AB)\to\Gamma(U_J\times_ST,\mathcal G_T)$ with $c_J(s\otimes b)=b\cdot(p^*s)|_{U_J\times_ST}$. Rewriting the source as $\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)\otimes_AB$ gives the displayed maps.

source.place: Proof, pullback cover and tensor identification of sections

proof.text: The maps $c_J$ commute with every Cech restriction map: restriction carries $s$ to its restriction, pullback commutes with restriction, and multiplication by the scalar $b$ is preserved. Since each Cech differential is an alternating sum of these restrictions, the $c_J$ therefore assemble into a cochain map $\gamma:K^\bullet\otimes_AB\to K_T^\bullet$.

The unit $\mathcal G\to Rp_*p^*\mathcal G$ is represented by the termwise map from the Cech resolution $\mathcal G\to C(U,\mathcal G)$ to the pulled-back Cech resolution $p_*C(U_T,\mathcal G_T)$: on each intersection $p^{-1}(U_J)=U_J\times_ST$, it sends a section $s$ to $p^*s$. The terms are $p_*$-acyclic: with $j_{J,T}:U_J\times_ST\to X_T$, the morphisms $j_{J,T}$ and $p\circ j_{J,T}=j_J\circ(U_J\times_ST\to U_J)$ are affine (open immersions of affine opens into the separated $X_T$, $X$, and a base change of the affine $T\to S$), so by [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] and [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] $Rp_*j_{J,T,*}=Rp_*Rj_{J,T,*}=R(p\circ j_{J,T})_*=(p\circ j_{J,T})_*$ on quasi-coherent modules; hence this termwise map represents the derived unit. Applying $f_*$ and the canonical composition isomorphism [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] $Rf_*Rp_*=R(f\circ p)_*=R(g\circ f_T)_*=Rg_*Rf_{T,*}$ gives the $A$-linear cochain map $K^\bullet\to K_T^\bullet$, $s\mapsto p^*s$, where $Rg_*\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}=g_*\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$ termwise because $g$ is affine and the terms are quasi-coherent [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi]. Under the adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint], the map represented by $\widetilde{K^\bullet}\to g_*\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$ has adjoint $Lg^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}\to g^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}\to\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$ by [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived]. The underived adjoint is the sheafification of the cochain map whose sections are the $c_J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], hence it is $\widetilde\gamma$. Therefore $\theta$ is the stated composite.
